cr_data.provenance: Harold Diamond, New York, NY, purchase, 1977; Andrew Crispo, New York, NY, 1979; Sotheby's, New York, NY, sale no. 7064, no. 158, 3 December 1997 (Source: Lynes, 1999)
remarks_1999: Not recorded Whitney Archive, Downtown Gallery Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks. Titled *Light Coming on the Plains* on Crispo label, implying completed in Texas and part of series bearing same title, see cat. nos. 209–11. O'Keeffe decided to work exclusively in black and white in late 1915, but about six months later returned to using color. "I began [fall of 1915] with charcoal and paper and decided not to use any color until it was impossible to do what I wanted to do in black and white. I believe it was June before I needed blue" (*Georgia O'Keeffe* [1976], unpaginated, text accompanying entry 1). Dated 1916 on basis of Stieglitz–O'Keeffe correspondence; completed in New York or Virginia before August move to Texas. See also cat. nos. 82, 83. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

description: Rippling blue lines create a rounded, cloud-like form at the center of the paper. Within the blue lines are soft, lighter blue and red forms punctuated by spots of green. The center of the form glows light yellow. Exposed white paper surrounds the image.
imageCaption: Image courtesy of a scanned transparency made for Georgia O'Keeffe: Catalogue Raisonné. This image has not been color proofed and may differ from the original. It will be replaced when newer photography becomes available.
